title: Evaluation of PV-1 as a marker of intestinal permeability in patients with liver cirrhosis
summary: Disorders of intestinal permeability (IP) are discussed as a risk factor for the development of bacterial translocation. The (51)Cr-EDTA permeability test has shown that intestinal permeability is impaired in 60% of patients with ascites, 31% of patients without ascites, and 4% of healthy controls. Another way to determine intestinal permeability is the time-consuming multisugar test. This test procedure can be used to examine the permeability of the small and large intestine. In a study by Vogt et al., for example, it was shown that the severity of liver disease correlated with the extent of intestinal permeability (small intestine). In a recently published study, we were able to show that plasma membrane vesicle protein 1 (PV-1), an endothelial cell-specific glycoprotein that is essential for the regulation of endothelial homeostasis and permeability of the gut-vascular barrier (GVB) and is therefore a potential marker of GVB, correlated with markers of bacterial translocation, namely endogenous endotoxin core IgA antibodies (EndoCAb) and LPS-binding protein (LBP), serum PV-1 concentrations were elevated in patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis, and elevated PV-1 levels were associated with poorer transplant-free survival in both univariate and multivariate analyses.
conditions: Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver

interventions.name:
All patients undergo a multisugar test. A single blood and urine sample is required from the test subjects for the examinations.
Once the participant has had sufficient time to consider participating in the study and has given their written consent after receiving detailed verbal and written inform

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Cirrhosis of the liver, defined by clinical, laboratory, or histological criteria.
2. Ascites °2 or °3 within the last 7 days
3. Hospitalization at the time of study inclusion
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) outside Milan or extrahepatic malignancy
2. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
3. Condition after TIPS placement
4. Hypersensitivity or allergies to sucrose, rhamnose, sucralose, erythritol, or lactulose.
5. Hereditary fructose intolerance
6. Presence of an existing or concomitant disease or general health condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, poses an unacceptable risk for participation in the study
7. Lactulose treatment within the last 72 hours.
